correctness.rationale: For r>L, the stationary voltage is the renewal mixture of the no-reset diffusion at an independent exponential age. The exact stationary generator identity reduces its mean to the age-averaged drift. Bounded-detuning SDE paths differ from Brownian paths by O(r^-1) in L1; the Brownian increment at exponential age has exact Laplace scale sqrt(D/r). The Laplace positive-part expectation has coefficient sqrt(D)/2 exp(-abs(xi)/sqrt(D)), and the remote kink contributes exponentially little. This proves a uniform O(r^-2) mean remainder. The frozen-recovery mean is a contraction with Lipschitz constant at most 1/(r-L), yielding the fixed-point expansion and global attraction. The embedded finite-volume script passed 28 checks; simulations do not prove the limit.

value.rationale: Resetting at a McKean switching threshold is dictated by the voltage piecewise-linear model rather than an arbitrary numerical slice. The explicit r^-1/2 parameter boundary layer and r^-3/2 response term identify a singular noise effect missed by smooth integer-power mean expansions; the exponential detuning shape predicts the gradual disappearance of the effect as reset voltage moves away. The fixed-point shift links a local fast-voltage kink to a macroscopic observable of the averaged recovery dynamics.
